questions.prompt: Explain why \(\{1,x,x^2\}\) is a basis for \(P_2\).
questions.answer: Every polynomial in \(P_2\) has the form \(a+bx+cx^2\), so it is a linear combination of 1, x, and \(x^2\). Thus the set spans \(P_2\). If \(a+bx+cx^2\) is the zero polynomial, then all coefficients must be zero: \(a=b=c=0\). Thus the set is linearly independent. Therefore \(\{1,x,x^2\}\) is a basis for \(P_2\).

The set \(\{1,x\}\) does not span \(P_2\) because it cannot produce \(x^2\). Every linear combination \(a\cdot1+b\cdot x\) has degree at most 1. Since \(x^2\) is in \(P_2\) but not in the span of \(\{1,x\}\), the set is not a basis for \(P_2\).

The set spans \(P_2\) because \(\{1,x,x^2\}\) already spans \(P_2\). However, it is not linearly independent because 1 + x is a linear combination of 1 and x. A basis must be both spanning and linearly independent. Therefore the set is not a basis.

questions.prompt: Show that \(\{1,x-1,(x-1)^2\}\) is a basis for \(P_2\).
questions.answer: There are three polynomials in \(P_2\), and \(\dim(P_2)=3\). It is enough to show linear independence. Suppose \(a\cdot1+b(x-1)+c(x-1)^2=0\). Expanding gives \(a+bx-b+c(x^2-2x+1)=cx^2+(b-2c)x+(a-b+c)\). For the zero polynomial, \(c=0\), then \(b-2c=b=0\), then \(a-b+c=a=0\). Therefore the set is linearly independent and hence a basis for \(P_2\).

questions.prompt: Give a standard basis for \(M_{2,2}(\mathbb R)\).
questions.answer: A standard basis is the set of matrices with one entry equal to 1 and all other entries 0. For \(M_{2,2}(\mathbb R)\), one such basis is {\(\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\), \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\), \(\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), \(\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\)}. Any \(2\times 2\) matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\) is a linear combination of these four matrices.

questions.prompt: Find coordinates of \(p(x)=3-2x+5x^2\) in the basis \(\{1,x,x^2\}\).
questions.answer: In the basis \(\{1,x,x^2\}\), the coordinates are the coefficients of 1, x, and \(x^2\) in that order. Since \(p(x)=3-2x+5x^2\), the coordinate vector is \((3, -2, 5)\).

questions.prompt: Find coordinates of \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\0&4\end{pmatrix}\) in the standard basis of \(M_{2,2}(\mathbb R)\) ordered as \(E_{11},E_{12},E_{21},E_{22}\).
questions.answer: With basis ordered as \(E_{11},E_{12},E_{21},E_{22}\), the coordinates are the entries of A in the same order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\0&4\end{pmatrix}\), the coordinate vector is \((2,-1,0,4)\).

\(P_1\) has dimension 2, so two linearly independent polynomials form a basis. Suppose \(a(1+x)+b(1-x)=0\). Expanding gives \((a+b)+(a-b)x=0\). Thus \(a+b=0\) and \(a-b=0\). Adding the equations gives \(2a=0\), so \(a=0\), and then \(b=0\). The set is linearly independent, so it is a basis for \(P_1\).

questions.prompt: Find a basis for the subspace of \(P_2\) consisting of polynomials p with \(p(0)\) = 0.
questions.answer: A polynomial in \(P_2\) has form \(a+bx+cx^2\). The condition \(p(0)=0\) gives \(a=0\). Therefore \(p(x)=bx+cx^2\). The polynomials \(x\) and \(x^2\) span the subspace and are linearly independent. Therefore a basis is \(\{x,x^2\}\).

questions.prompt: A learner says \(\{1,x,x^2,x^3\}\) is a basis for \(P_2\) because it contains \(\{1,x,x^2\}\). Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: The polynomial \(x^3\) is not in \(P_2\), because \(P_2\) contains only polynomials of degree at most 2. A basis for a vector space must consist of vectors from that vector space. Therefore \(\{1,x,x^2,x^3\}\) cannot be a basis for \(P_2\).
